purpose: Design and test-venue constraints only; not legal advice or permission to operate.

requirements: floorboard designed to be stood upon
not greater than 60 inches deep and 18 inches wide
designed to transport only one person
electric propulsion system averaging less than 1000 watts
maximum propulsion-only speed on paved level surface no more than 20 mph

operation_constraints.highway_exception: Class II or Class IV bikeway
darkness_equipment: white forward light visible from 300 feet, or qualifying operator-mounted substitute
red rear reflector visible from 500 feet, or qualifying operator-mounted substitute
white or yellow side reflectors visible from 200 feet, or qualifying operator-mounted substitute

classification_boundary.rule: Do not assume CVC 21290-21296 public-operation rules apply unless the final vehicle actually satisfies the CVC 313.5 definition.
classification_boundary.reason: The statutory definition constrains the propulsion system itself; a low-speed ride mode alone is not treated by this project as proof of classification.

terrain_reference.character: natural woodlands, vegetation, neighborhood park trails and meadow

worcester_park.role_in_project: terrain and product-requirement inspiration only unless Town rules change or written authorization is obtained

preferred: private property with owner permission and controlled access
closed or controlled test area where vehicle operation is expressly authorized
bench and unpowered fixtures before any powered ground testing
do_not_assume_authorized: other Los Gatos Town parks or trails
public roads merely because Shasta mode is selected
test_venue_policy.requirement: Before any powered ground test, record venue owner/jurisdiction, permission basis, surface, pedestrian separation, emergency stop plan and applicable operating restrictions.

trail_private_authorized.goal: maximize trail capability for private or expressly authorized terrain

public_road_oriented_derivative.goal: study a separate hardware architecture that can demonstrably satisfy the applicable public-road category if neighborhood road use remains a product requirement
unresolved: how California interprets averaging less than 1000 watts for the final propulsion system
whether selected motors/controllers/battery architecture can fit the statutory definition
local street/bikeway restrictions at the intended route
whether a separate lower-power hardware derivative is preferable to compromising trail architecture

design_implications: Do not optimize X1 around Worcester Park as a physical test site.
Keep lights/reflectors as a real product requirement if any public-road-oriented derivative is pursued.
Do not let a 2.7 m/s Shasta software cap stand in for vehicle classification.
Preserve the option for a trail-first private/authorized-use X1 and a distinct lower-power public-road-oriented derivative.
Public-use legality and venue permission must be rechecked immediately before physical testing because rules can change.
